evidence.quote: It is unknown whether SAXENDA causes thyroid C-cell tumors, including medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC), in humans, as the human relevance of liraglutide-induced rodent thyroid C-cell tumors has not been determined [see Warnings and Precautions (5.1), Nonclinical Toxicology (13.1)]

Cases of MTC in patients treated with liraglutide have been reported in the postmarketing period; the data in these reports are insufficient to establish or exclude a causal relationship between MTC and liraglutide use in humans.

response.reasoning: The claim states that SAXENDA has no risk of thyroid tumors, but the label excerpts mention the risk of thyroid C-cell tumors, including medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC), in patients treated with SAXENDA. The excerpts also mention that cases of MTC have been reported in patients treated with liraglutide, and that it is unknown whether SAXENDA will cause thyroid tumors or MTC in humans. Therefore, the claim is contradicted by the label excerpts.
